en: become short of breath; breathe faster

examples.en: I ran up the stairs and got out of breath.
When I get nervous, my breathing gets faster.
If you get short of breath, take a short rest before going on.

examples.ko: 달리기를 하다 보니 숨이 점점 가빠지기 시작했어요.
examples.en: As I kept running, my breathing began to get heavier.

examples.ko: 가슴이 답답하고 숨이 가빠져서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My chest felt tight and I was short of breath, so I went to the hospital.

examples.ko: 발표 때 갑자기 말이 빨라지고 숨이 가빠질까 봐 걱정이에요.
examples.en: I worry that during the presentation I will suddenly talk fast and get short of breath.

explain: 주로 '숨이 가빠지다, 호흡이 가빠지다'의 모양으로 써요. 이미 숨이 찬 상태는 '숨이 가쁘다'이고, 가빠지다는 점점 그렇게 변해 간다는 느낌이에요. 'ㅡ'가 빠져서 '가빠요, 가빠졌어요'가 돼요.
explain_en: It mostly appears as '숨이 가빠지다' or '호흡이 가빠지다'. '숨이 가쁘다' describes the state of already being out of breath, while this word means gradually getting into that state. The ㅡ drops out, giving '가빠요' and '가빠졌어요'.

examples.en: The mask strap rubs against the back of my ears and hurts.
A mosquito bit the back of my ear and it keeps itching.
My glasses are small, so the backs of my ears hurt.
It was so cold that even the backs of my ears turned red.
At the beach, only the backs of my ears got sunburned.

examples.ko: 제 말을 귓등으로 듣지 말고 잘 들어 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't brush off what I say and listen carefully.

explain: 몸의 부위로 쓸 때는 안경다리나 마스크 끈이 닿는 귀 쪽을 말해요. '귓등으로 듣다'라는 표현으로도 나와요.

phrases.example: 선생님 말씀을 귓등으로 듣다가 숙제를 놓쳤어요.
phrases.en: I half-listened to the teacher and missed the homework.
phrases.nuance_ko: 듣기는 해도 마음에 담지 않고 흘려듣는다는 뜻이라 비난하는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hearing something without taking it in, and carries a tone of criticism.
phrases.en_equiv: let it go in one ear and out the other

explain_en: As a body part it refers to the area of the ear where glasses arms or mask straps rest. It also appears in the expression '귓등으로 듣다'.

examples.en: Grandfather wore a magoja over his hanbok.
On Seollal, my father wore a vest and a magoja.
The magoja has pretty buttons on it.
A magoja is nice with winter hanbok because it's warm.
Wearing a magoja, you look dignified.

examples.ko: 저고리 위에 마고자를 하나 더 입었어요.
examples.en: I put on a magoja over the jeogori as one more layer.

explain: 남자 한복에서 저고리 위에 덧입는 겉옷이에요. 조끼, 두루마기와 헷갈리기 쉬운데, 마고자는 깃이 없고 앞에 단추를 달아 입는 옷이에요. 명절이나 결혼식 같은 날에 한복을 입을 때 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: It is an outer layer worn over the jeogori in men's hanbok. It is easy to confuse with the vest or the durumagi, but the magoja has no collar and fastens with buttons at the front. You see it when people wear hanbok on holidays or at weddings.

examples.en: I'm so cold that my whole body is shivering.

examples.ko: 강아지가 천둥 소리에 바들바들 떨고 있어요.
examples.en: The puppy is trembling at the sound of thunder.
My hands were shaking before the presentation.

examples.ko: 할아버지가 지팡이를 잡은 손을 바들바들 떠세요.
examples.en: My grandfather's hand holding the cane is trembling.

examples.ko: 겁이 나서 다리가 바들바들 떨려 못 걸었어요.
examples.en: I was so scared that my legs shook and I couldn't walk.

examples.ko: 바들바들 떨지 말고 심호흡을 해 봐요.
examples.en: Don't shake like that, try taking a deep breath.

explain: 주로 '떨다, 떨리다'와 함께 써요. '벌벌'이 더 널리 쓰이고, '바들바들'은 작고 가늘게 계속 떠는 느낌이에요. 추위, 무서움, 긴장, 힘이 없을 때 모두 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It mostly goes with '떨다' or '떨리다'. '벌벌' is more widely used, while '바들바들' suggests small, thin, continuous trembling. It fits cold, fear, nerves or weakness.

examples.ko: 너무 지쳐서 그는 비척거리며 집에 들어왔어요.
examples.en: He was so exhausted that he staggered into the house.

examples.ko: 오래 아픈 할머니가 비척거리면서 방을 나오셨어요.
examples.en: My grandmother, who has been ill for a long time, came out of her room tottering.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 갑자기 비척거려서 제가 팔을 잡았어요.
examples.en: He suddenly staggered, so I grabbed his arm.

examples.ko: 산에서 내려오는 길에 다리가 풀려 비척거렸어요.
examples.en: My legs gave way on the way down the mountain and I stumbled along.
Why are you wobbling like that? Are you sick?

examples.ko: 비척거리지 말고 여기 앉아서 좀 쉬세요.
examples.en: Don't totter around; sit here and rest a bit.

explain: '비틀거리다', '휘청거리다'와 비슷하지만, 힘이 없거나 몸이 안 좋아서 제대로 걷지 못하는 느낌이 강해요. 대화에서는 '비틀거리다'로 바꿔 말해도 돼요. '비척대다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is similar to '비틀거리다' and '휘청거리다', but it strongly suggests someone too weak or unwell to walk properly. In conversation you can swap in '비틀거리다'. '비척대다' means the same thing.

examples.en: The child is holding back tears, pushing out his lips.

examples.ko: 기분이 상했는지 동생이 계속 입을 삐죽거려요.
examples.en: My younger sibling keeps pouting, probably upset.
Don't pout, say it in words.
It was cute to see my friend pouting.
She pouted because she didn't get praised.

examples.ko: 그 아이는 서운하면 삐죽거려서 금방 알 수 있어요.
examples.en: When that child feels hurt she pouts, so it's easy to tell.

explain: 서운하거나 울음이 날 때 입술을 내미는 동작이에요. '입을 삐죽거리다'처럼 자주 쓰고, 같은 뜻으로 '삐죽이다'나 '삐죽대다'도 있어요.
explain_en: It is the movement of pushing out the lips when feeling hurt or about to cry, often as '입을 삐죽거리다'. '삐죽이다' and '삐죽대다' also exist with the same meaning.

examples.en: I fell and got a scratch on my knee.
Please put ointment on the scratch.
I went through a thorn bush and my legs are covered in scratches.

examples.ko: 작은 생채기라도 소독은 꼭 해야 해요.
examples.en: Even a small scratch needs to be disinfected.

examples.ko: 친구의 말 한마디가 마음에 생채기를 냈어요.
examples.en: One word from my friend left a scratch on my heart.
A scratch mark remained on the child's face.

explain: '상처'보다 작고 가벼운, 긁히거나 할퀸 상처에 써요. '마음의 생채기'처럼 사소해 보여도 아픈 마음의 상처를 비유할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It is smaller and lighter than '상처' (wound), used for a scrape or a claw mark. It is also used figuratively, as in '마음의 생채기', for a hurt that looks small but still stings.

examples.en: The child grabbed my sleeve and wouldn't let go.
I wiped my tears away with my sleeve.
The sleeve of the hanbok fluttered in the wind.
Kimchi broth got on my sleeve.
The end of the sleeve was frayed, so I took it to be repaired.
The clothes are big, so the sleeves hang down over the backs of my hands.

explain: '소매'가 가장 일상적인 말이고, '소맷자락'은 늘어진 소매 부분을 느낌 있게 말할 때 써요. 한복이나 이야기 속 장면에서 잘 어울려요. 소매의 끝부분만 가리킬 때는 '소매 끝'이라고 해도 돼요.
explain_en: '소매' is the everyday word, while '소맷자락' describes the hanging part of a sleeve with more feeling. It suits hanbok and story scenes. To point only to the end of a sleeve, you can also say '소매 끝'.

examples.ko: 팔에 벌레가 기어가는 것처럼 스멀스멀 간지러워요.
examples.en: My arm feels creepy-itchy, as if a bug were crawling on it.

examples.ko: 등 뒤에서 이상한 기운이 스멀스멀 올라왔어요.
examples.en: A strange feeling crept up from behind my back.
An anxious feeling is slowly creeping up in me.
Smoke crept slowly into the room.
My scalp felt creepy-itchy, so I kept scratching it.

examples.ko: 아침이 되자 안개가 스멀스멀 퍼지고 있어요.
examples.en: As morning came, fog was slowly spreading.

explain: 벌레가 살갗 위를 기어가는 듯 근질근질한 느낌을 말해요. 비유로 불안, 연기, 안개 같은 것이 슬그머니 번지거나 올라오는 모습에도 자주 써요. '스멀스멀 올라오다', '스멀스멀 퍼지다'처럼 어울려요.
explain_en: It describes a tingly, itchy feeling as if a bug were crawling on the skin. Figuratively it is also used for anxiety, smoke or fog creeping in and spreading. It pairs with '스멀스멀 올라오다' and '스멀스멀 퍼지다'.

examples.ko: 감기가 다 나은 줄 알았는데 재발했어요.
examples.en: I thought my cold was gone, but it came back.

examples.ko: 허리 통증이 자꾸 재발해서 병원에 갔어요.
examples.en: My back pain kept recurring, so I went to the hospital.
What do we do if the same problem recurs?

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 병이 재발할 수 있다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said the illness could come back.
I take my medicine regularly so that it does not come back.
That accident happened again, and everyone was shocked.

explain: '재발하다'는 한 번 나았던 병이나 사라졌던 문제가 다시 생길 때 써요. 병, 버릇, 사고에 어울리고, 처음 생기는 일에는 '발생하다'를 써요. '다시 생기다'보다 의학이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 재발하다 is for an illness, habit or problem that was gone and comes back. For something happening the first time, use '발생하다'. It appears in medicine and news more often than the plain '다시 생기다'.

examples.en: Tears streamed down the child's cheeks.
The cup tilted and the water poured out.
Sweat is running down my forehead.
The candle wax melted and ran down.
Raindrops trickle down the window.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보다가 눈물이 주르르 났어요.
examples.en: Tears rolled down while I watched the sad movie.

explain: 눈물, 땀, 빗물이 한 줄기로 길게 흘러내리는 모양을 말해요. '주르륵'과 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. 계속 내리는 비는 '주룩주룩'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It describes tears, sweat or rain running down in a single stream. You can swap it with '주르륵'. Rain that keeps falling is '주룩주룩'.

examples.ko: 삼촌이 사고로 척수를 다쳐서 휠체어를 타요.
examples.en: My uncle injured his spinal cord in an accident and uses a wheelchair.
The spinal cord is inside the spine.
The doctor suggested a spinal cord test.

examples.ko: 척수가 손상되면 감각이 사라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If the spinal cord is damaged, feeling can be lost.

examples.ko: 척수에 문제가 생기면 몸을 움직이기 어려워요.
examples.en: If there is a problem with the spinal cord, it is hard to move the body.

examples.ko: 척수의 신경을 다시 살리는 연구가 진행 중이에요.
examples.en: Research on reviving the nerves of the spinal cord is under way.

explain: '척추'는 등뼈이고 '척수'는 그 안을 지나는 신경 다발이에요. 이름이 비슷해도 뼈와 신경으로 달라요. 의료 이야기에서 '척수 손상', '척수 신경'처럼 써요.
explain_en: '척추' is the backbone, and '척수' is the bundle of nerves running through it. The names are similar, but one is bone and the other is nerve. In medical talk you see '척수 손상' and '척수 신경'.

examples.en: I was nervous before the exam, so I took a cheongsimhwan.

examples.ko: 청심환 한 알이면 마음이 좀 가라앉을까요?
examples.en: Would one cheongsimhwan pill calm me down a bit?
You can buy cheongsimhwan at a pharmacy.
The cheongsimhwan didn't make me sleepy.
I might take at least a cheongsimhwan before the presentation.
My grandmother believes cheongsimhwan works.

explain: 한방에서 온 환약으로, 긴장되거나 놀랐을 때 마음을 가라앉히려고 먹는 약으로 알려져 있어요. 시험, 면접, 발표 앞에서 '청심환 먹어야겠다'라고 농담처럼 말하기도 해요. 약이니까 먹기 전에 약사에게 물어보세요.
explain_en: It is a pill from traditional Korean medicine, known as something taken to calm nerves when anxious or startled. People joke '청심환 먹어야겠다' before exams, interviews or presentations. Since it is medicine, ask a pharmacist before taking it.

examples.ko: 췌장은 배 안쪽 깊은 곳에 있는 장기예요.
examples.en: The pancreas is an organ located deep inside the belly.

examples.ko: 건강검진에서 췌장 수치가 조금 높게 나왔어요.
examples.en: My pancreas levels came out a little high in the health checkup.

examples.ko: 췌장에서 인슐린이 나온다고 과학 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned in science class that insulin comes from the pancreas.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님은 췌장도 같이 검사해 보자고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor suggested we check the pancreas as well.

examples.ko: 기름진 음식을 많이 먹으면 췌장에 부담이 돼요.
examples.en: Eating a lot of greasy food puts a burden on the pancreas.
Managing blood sugar is easier when your pancreas is healthy.

explain: 병원이나 뉴스에서 많이 듣는 장기 이름이고, 병명에서는 '췌장암'처럼 뒤에 말이 붙어요. 혈당과 소화 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: This organ name is heard mostly in hospitals and the news, and in disease names it takes a suffix, as in '췌장암' (pancreatic cancer). It comes up often in talk about blood sugar and digestion.

examples.en: Fortunately it's not serious, just a bruise.
I fell on the stairs and bruised my knee.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 타박상에는 냉찜질이 좋다고 하셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor said a cold compress is good for bruises.
I collided while playing soccer and got a bruise on my thigh.
Because of the contusion, I got a big bruise.

examples.ko: 가벼운 타박상이라 며칠 쉬면 나을 거래요.
examples.en: They say it's a mild bruise, so it'll heal after a few days' rest.

explain: 부딪히거나 맞아서 피부는 찢어지지 않았지만 속에 멍이 들고 붓는 상처를 말해요. 긁히거나 쓸린 상처는 '찰과상'이라고 해요. 병원이나 뉴스에서 쓰는 말이고, 일상에서는 '멍들었다'라고 말하기도 해요.
explain_en: It is an injury from a hit or collision where the skin is not broken but the tissue beneath is bruised and swollen. A scrape on the surface is called '찰과상'. It is the word used at hospitals and in the news, while in daily talk people may just say '멍들었다'.
